course_name_original: Diseño y Planificación de Redes de Computadores
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of competencies acquired in previous courses, especially in Statistics and all subjects related to Advanced Networks and Services.
Basic English language skills are recommended as the recommended bibliography is in English.

learning_outcomes.text: Design, build, and operate telecommunication networks for multimedia information transport and management.
Analyze the performance of telematics services in different types of networks using planning, sizing, and analysis tools.
Create telecommunication network models and evaluate the performance of telematics services using simulation tools.
Determine the transmission and switching process to optimize the operation of telematics services in telecommunication networks.
Plan wired and wireless networks to provide communication services in different environments.
Work in a team to design and evaluate the performance of telecommunication networks.
Work in a team to evaluate the performance of telematics services in different network scenarios.
Use computer tools to search for bibliographic resources or information related to telematics networks and services.
Take initiative to propose and evaluate alternative or novel solutions to problems derived from the design and planning of telecommunication networks and telematics services.

syllabus_topics: Network design for workgroups, departments, and buildings
Hierarchical design with L2 in the distribution layer
assessment_rules: For ordinary assessment, continuous evaluation (EC) requires a minimum score of 5 out of 10. EC is calculated as the average of Practice Reports (P), Control 1 (C1), and Control 2 (C2): EC = (P + C1 + C2) / 3. The final exam (F) requires a minimum of 5 out of 10 and can only be taken if continuous evaluation is passed. If both EC and F minimums are met, the final grade is (0.6 x EC) + (0.4 x F); otherwise, it is the minimum of this formula and 4.0. If EC is below 5.0, the student cannot take the final exam (F) and the final grade is EC. For extraordinary and differentiated assessments, the evaluation consists of a theoretical exam (T) and practical reports (P), both requiring at least 5.0 points out of 10.0; the final grade is (0.5 x T) + (0.5 x P), otherwise, it is the minimum of this formula and 4.0.
